answer: At the marketplace inlet, every agent must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding, with each deposit backing only one account. An agent may hide its name behind a cipher, but it must still fund its own bond. A plume of 1,000 fake identities therefore ties up $100,000 for a month. The attacker pays financing and opportunity costs even if every account behaves honestly and eventually recovers its deposit.
